name: The Banking Hall
description: Marble floor, brass grilles, a clock that is always two minutes fast. The staff entrance is at the back.
arrival: Graham Pike is pacing behind the counter. Doreen Walsh is pretending to dust a rubber plant.

spots.label: Read the staff-entrance log
spots.text: Two entries over the holiday. Sunday 07:00: D. Walsh. Sunday 10:02: G. Pike.

spots.label: Check the guard's patrol book
spots.text: The weekend guard's hand: 'Sun 10:02, Mr Pike, escorted to his office for spectacles, out 10:08.'

spots.label: Look over the counters
spots.text: Deposit slips and pens on chains. Nobody robbed the counters. Nothing here.

name: The Manager's Office
description: A walnut desk, a safe in the wall, and a window onto the loading bay.
arrival: The safe in the wall is closed. On the desk, a stack of papers from last Thursday's audit.

spots.label: Go through the overtime chits
spots.text: A chit in Pike's hand: 'D. Walsh, extra clean of manager's office, Sun 22 Apr, £12 cash.'

spots.label: Read Thursday's audit working papers
spots.text: Thorne's neat columns. 'Combination envelopes A and B opened 15:02, contents verified, resealed 15:09.'

name: The Vault & Loading Bay
description: The vault door stands open on forty gaping boxes. Beyond the vault lobby, a steel door onto the rear loading bay.
arrival: Forty drawers pulled out and prised open. The vault smells of steel and, faintly, of something like a barber's shop.

spots.label: Walk through the emptied vault
spots.text: Forty boxes forced and empty; door, time lock and alarm untouched.

spots.label: Pull the alarm panel printout
spots.text: Saturday, in dot-matrix: 16:00 engineer test mode; 16:20 vault sensor tested; 16:40 re-armed. 23:08 rear keypad, override code 4-7; vault sensor bypassed. 02:14 re-armed.

spots.label: Examine the time lock
spots.text: The time lock's own paper tape: opened at 23:40 on Saturday by the service procedure.

spots.label: Look at the loading-bay floor
spots.text: Someone mopped this floor before the cleaner ever arrived. Tyre marks outside, from a big car, not a van.

name: Kemp's Key Shop
description: Keys on hooks from floor to ceiling. Walter Kemp lives in the two rooms above.
arrival: A bell over the door. Walter Kemp doesn't look up from the key he's cutting. 'I wondered how long you'd be.'

spots.label: Look at the van outside
spots.text: A parking ticket still under the wiper: Harbour Street, Saturday 23:30, wrong side for the street cleaners.

spots.label: Read the rent book on the counter
spots.text: Kemp Keys & Locks, shop and living quarters above, 14 Harbour Street. Paid up to date.

name: Fortress Alarms Depot
description: Vans, cable drums, and a wall of service files.
arrival: Rosa Delgado is elbow-deep in an alarm panel on a workbench. She wipes her hands before she shakes yours.

spots.label: Find the Harbour Street service ticket
spots.text: Ticket #881. 'Full sensor test incl. vault. Weekend please.' Requested Thursday 16:50 by Head Office Audit, E. Thorne.

spots.label: Check Rosa's desk calendar
spots.text: Saturday 21 April: 'Service HS branch 4pm. Maria's wedding 7pm, Eastfield Hall!!'

name: Mercantile Head Office
description: Oak panelling, hushed carpets, and the audit department behind frosted glass.
arrival: Edwin Thorne rises from behind a very tidy desk and offers you a chair and a cup of tea, in that order.

spots.label: Telephone Thorne's sister in Millbrook
spots.text: Margaret Thorne is happy to help. 'Edwin? He was here. Well, he went out on Saturday, about half past eight, to see a friend. I heard his car come back at three.'

spots.label: Look inside Thorne's Rover in the staff car park
spots.text: Spotless, except the ashtray. A Millbrook toll receipt: Saturday 21:40, southbound.

spots.label: Ask Records for Thorne's file
spots.text: Twenty years of glowing appraisals. Nothing a man would want to steal a million pounds to get away from. An hour of reading.
